clue.text: Poor Alice — very mad and reckless

indicators.note: poor here means in a sorry state, so the letters of the three words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sympathises with a girl called Alice who is both thoroughly unhinged and rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' reads as pity for Alice, but it signals an anagram of ALICE VERY MAD, all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy-go-lucky person who takes no heed of consequences is reckless, a synonym.

clue.text: Coward put a leading player in divine location

indicators.note: in tells us the phrase a leading player is to be placed inside the letters for divine

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a learned divine or clergyman
the leading player in a show or team is its star

explanation.surface: Someone places a principal actor in a holy place, as Noel Coward might stage it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like the playwright Noel Coward, but it is the definition: a base coward. 'location' simply says where the pieces go.
explanation.definitionFit: A dastard is an old word for a mean, sneaking person lacking courage, a craven.

clue.text: Vitality mostly found in Spanish port

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word but not all, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: vitality means vigor (US spelling of vigour), energy and strength

explanation.surface: Energy is found in plenty in a harbour city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed word is the American spelling VIGOR; dropping its final R leaves the Galician port city.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigo is a major Atlantic seaport city in Galicia, north-west Spain.

clue.text: Screen a dry man covered in parasites

indicators.note: covered in means the following parasites wrap around the a-plus-dry-man pieces

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects
TT stands for teetotal, a man who is dry and drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A sober chap is shielded from view while crawling with vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry man' is TT, the crossword convention for a teetotaller; it goes with A inside LICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a crisscross framework of strips used as a screen, for instance over a window.

clue.text: Judge a bishop without incisiveness

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the letters for bishop surround those for incisiveness

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
incisiveness, sharpness of wit, is bite

explanation.surface: A judge says a certain bishop lacks any sharpness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here it has its old sense of outside; RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's formal title.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone appointed to settle a dispute, effectively a referee or adjudicator.

clue.text: Salt therapy

definitions.meaning: to salt meat or fish is to preserve it by drying or smoking
a treatment or remedy that restores health

explanation.definitionFit: Curing meat means preserving it with salt, and a remedy that heals an illness is the other sense.

clue.text: Withdraw pamphlet on scripture

indicators.note: on here means placed next to, so the pamphlet follows the scripture letters

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject that teaches scripture
a tract is a short religious or political pamphlet

explanation.surface: Someone takes back a leaflet about the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is British shorthand for religious education, the school subject once called scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back or recant it.

clue.text: Seamstresses may fail to follow the story

definitions.meaning: sewing women might literally mislay a strand of cotton
become confused about where a narrative or argument is going

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for getting lost in a narrative borrows a literal mishap with sewing cotton.

clue.text: Look out for uneven pavements!

parts.note: a warning sign about broken paving, read as the everyday phrase urging care where you tread

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means take care, literally mind where your foot goes, a fitting warning about bumpy paths.

clue.text: First seen working as a builder, say

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase for working as a builder is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a builder at work is on site, on the building site

explanation.surface: A tradesman notices something the first time he is at work on a building.
explanation.walkthrough: ON SITE, where a builder works, sounds the same as ON SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on sight means doing it as soon as it is first spotted, like reading music at first view.

clue.text: A bitter affliction for a priest

indicators.note: affliction suggests something troubled and disordered, so the letters of a and bitter are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clergyman suffers a painful hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affliction' signals an anagram of A BITTER; 'for a priest' is the definition, the cap a priest wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap with three ridges worn by Roman Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Cutback many find a testing experience

parts.note: read as two words: axe, to chop, written back to front
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, standing for many

explanation.surface: Many people find spending cuts a trying ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutback' looks like one word for a spending reduction, but split it: AXE (to chop) written back to front gives EXA, then M (a thousand, many).
explanation.definitionFit: An examination is a test of knowledge, and sitting one is a trying ordeal.

clue.text: The outlook from Kiev is tactically good

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: The view from the Ukrainian capital offers a strategic advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside kieV IS TActically; 'good' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a view or prospect, especially a long one seen from a height.

clue.text: Married a Catholic producing brandy

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A wedding to a Catholic results in some strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is a spirit distilled from the skins and pips left after grapes are pressed, a kind of brandy.

clue.text: Hesitate to get a curling-iron

definitions.meaning: a tool that puts waves into hair

explanation.definitionFit: Dithering is one sense; a device that puts waves into hair is a thing that waves.

clue.text: It may grow in a small enclosure

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Something might sprout inside a little fenced area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here, not a container signal: the pieces simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar tree, which is something that grows.

clue.text: Sadly the yard appears to fill with water

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of the and yard are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unfortunately the garden seems to be getting flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' signals an anagram of THE YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To hydrate something is to supply it with water or cause it to take water in.

clue.text: Dish master returned to reflective German

indicators.note: returned means the word for master is turned back to front

parts.note: sir is a respectful word for a master

indicators.note: reflective means this name looks the same in a mirror, reading identically either way

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A teacher went back to a thoughtful man from Germany for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR read backwards gives RIS; OTTO is a palindrome, so 'reflective' just confirms it reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Board gets a union leader representation

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging

indicators.note: leader means only the first letter of union is taken

explanation.surface: A company board gets a union head to represent workers.
explanation.walkthrough: TABLEAU is a picture or scene, a vivid representation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking scene or picture, often a group posed to depict something.

clue.text: Unladen vessel ornately adorned

annotationWithheld.why: Unladen vessel ornately adorned (7): BARQUE around O, but 'Unladen' must both supply O (nothing) and signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Not certain if Sam has gone to Arabia

parts.note: Uncle Sam is the figure who personifies the US
AR is an abbreviation of Arabia or Arabic

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Uncle Sam has travelled to the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam leads to UNCLE through Uncle Sam, the personification of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is doubtful or uncertain.

clue.text: Walk round umpire to make introduction

indicators.note: round means the walking word goes around the umpire word

parts.note: to pace is to walk with measured steps
ref, short for referee, is an umpire

explanation.surface: Someone strolls around an official to open proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: A preface is the opening section of a book, its introductory foreword.

clue.text: Rod and Tom find it a stinker

parts.note: a rod and a pole are both long thin staffs
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Two men, Rod and Tom, find something smelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod and Tom' look like two men's names; they are a pole and a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a weasel-like animal notorious for its foul-smelling secretions.

clue.text: No age is free from dire sufferings

indicators.note: free means the letters of no age is are released from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Nobody of any age escapes terrible pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' signals an anagram of NO AGE IS; 'from' only links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonies are extreme physical or mental pains.

clue.text: Combined corps hardly ever seen

parts.note: two army corps are joined: RA, the Royal Artillery
and RE, the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A joint military force is seldom spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Artillery) and RE (Royal Engineers) are two British Army corps, here put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is uncommon and seldom met with.

clue.text: Relative dimensions of a fish-plate

definitions.meaning: proportion between a model or map and the real thing
one of the small horny plates covering a fish's skin

explanation.definitionFit: A map's ratio to the real ground is one sense; the small protective plates on a fish's body are the other.

clue.text: Skips needed by a brewery

definitions.meaning: the dried flowers used to flavour beer

explanation.definitionFit: Small jumps are one sense; the bitter flowers that flavour beer are the other.

clue.text: Leg-show for a Frenchman in Liberia

indicators.note: in places the letter for a Frenchman inside the abbreviation for Liberia

parts.note: Lib. is an abbreviation of Liberia
M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, a French gentleman

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in West Africa puts on a display of leg.
explanation.walkthrough: M, short for Monsieur, goes inside LIB, an abbreviation of Liberia.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg is one of the body's limbs, an arm or leg.

clue.text: Contract means that Kelvin can retire

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

indicators.note: retire means draw back, so the word for can is read backwards

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: An agreement allows a man called Kelvin to stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: brows knit when they draw together. 'retire' turns the can word round.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit the brows is to draw them together, so to knit is to tighten or draw in.

clue.text: Get airman to join vocal ensemble

parts.note: AC is aircraftman, the lowest rank of airman in the RAF
quire is an old spelling of choir, a group of singers

explanation.surface: A pilot decides to sign up with a singing group.
explanation.walkthrough: AC is aircraftman, the RAF's lowest rank; QUIRE is the archaic spelling of choir.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire is to obtain or come to own.

clue.text: Imprison criminal? Splendid!

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is a criminal
fine means splendid, excellent

explanation.surface: Someone cheers at the thought of locking up a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine someone is to shut them in and restrict their freedom, as a jail does.

clue.text: Houseman declares they're in the EU

parts.note: a member is someone who sits in the House of Commons, a man of the House
to declare is to state

explanation.surface: A junior hospital doctor names those countries that belong to the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houseman' suggests a junior hospital doctor, but here it is a member of the House (of Commons).
explanation.definitionFit: Countries belonging to the European Union are called its member states.
